title: Two preventable claim burns in one session, same root shape

incidents.error: Archived run/, loop_state/, broker_state/ but missed evidence/ -> ARTIFACT_ALREADY_EXISTS.
incidents.validated: that the three directories I knew about were clear
incidents.not_validated: the COMPLETE set of persist() targets, derivable from the source in one grep

incidents.error: Authorization lacked voyage_service_label -> KeyError after the launch claim was written.
incidents.validated: the authorization against validate_authorization, which PASSED
incidents.not_validated: the authorization against integration()'s live branch, which reads a key no gate checks

common_root: Both times I validated against ONE layer and treated that as sufficient. A passing gate is evidence the gate is satisfied, not evidence the run will proceed. Where a one-shot claim is written before the real work begins, the pre-flight must model the CONSUMER path end to end, derived from the source rather than from notes or memory.
corrective_rule: Before any dispatch that writes a one-shot claim: (1) grep the source for every write target and every input-key access on the path AFTER the claim; (2) satisfy or clear each one; (3) only then dispatch. Cost of the check: one grep. Cost of skipping it: a burned attempt.
what_went_right: Both failures were caught immediately, cost little or nothing, consumed no research work, and left complete evidence. The probe-before-dispatch discipline that preceded Route D attempt 1 is the pattern to keep -- it just needs to cover harness state and input keys, not only the provider path.
